tool.name: mcp__pixellab__pixelart_workbench
tool.description:
Run one pixel-art command on a drawing or image you already made. This is
the engine's own command line: it checks work, explains it and improves it.

Commands: check and explain (read-only):
- lint <id> [--rules outline_gap,orphan_pixel,…] — pixel-art defects, each
  naming the node and command that drew them
- inspect <id> --region x0,y0,x1,y1 --scale 10 — a zoomed crop with its
  exact colours
- measure <id> --at x,y — what is at a pixel and who drew it
- explain <id> — resolved geometry, per-command footprints, before rendering
- motion / storyboard / silhouette / reveal / clusters / parts <id> — reports
- score <id> — a 0-100 pixel-art discipline score with a breakdown
- compare <id> <id> — two results side by side
Improve (returns a NEW drawing id):
- shade <id> --band 2 --light=-1,-1 — banded shading along a colour ramp
- selout <id> — selective outlining; reoutline / clean-lines / aa / mirror
- cluster <id> --at x,y --action recolor --color <name> — one guarded cluster
- repair <id> — deterministic cleanup of drift, strays, fringe and noise
Sheets and frames (returns a NEW image id):
- split <image> --grid 3x3 — a sprite sheet, strip or grid as an animation,
  one frame per cell (columns x rows)
- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures
  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation
- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a
  4x4 block (a sticker, a print); nothing is redrawn
A result comes back as an image in the reply AND as a no-auth URL the reply
prints, `/mcp/pixel-tools/<id>/image.png` (`frames.png` for the frames of a
multi-frame one) — so a sheet you joined is both readable inline and
downloadable. Sheets hold at most 1024 px a side; `join` refuses a larger
one rather than shrinking the art, and says how many frames do fit.
Craft operations need colour ramps: run `extract-palette <id>` first, then
pass `--ramps skin=dark,mid,light`.
Authoring: `edit <id> --changes '[…]'` applies exact pixel operations and
`draw <id> --recipe '{…}'` builds or revises a layered scene; both take JSON
whose fields are NOT listed here. Colours in that JSON are always `#RRGGBB`
or `#RRGGBBAA` with alpha `00` or `ff` — `rgb()` and bare hex are refused,
and nothing strips the `#`, since argv is a JSON list rather than a shell
line. Every `edit` change carries `operation`, `layer`, `frames` (ONE-based)
and `reason`; coordinates are zero-based and a `region` is `[x0,y0,x1,y1]`
inclusive. Then its own fields: `patch_pixels` takes `pixels`, a list of
`[x,y,expected,replacement]` (1-10000, each assigned only where the pixel
already holds `expected`, so a mismatch fails the pass); `copy_region` takes
`source_layer`, `source_frame`, `region`, `at` `[x,y]`; `map_colors` takes
`region` and `colors` `{"#from":"#to"}` (alpha must match); `flood_fill`
`seed`/`expected`/`color`; `brush` `points` plus `color`; `outline` `mode`
(outside|inside|recolor|erase). The full contracts and any command's flags
are one free call away: `describe edits | paint | outline | draw | animation
| motion | scenes | review`, `<command> -h`, `describe cli`.
Free for subscribers.

PixelLab AI-powered pixel art generation service.

Use of this service is subject to PixelLab's Terms of Service:
https://pixellab.ai/termsofservice

This MCP server provides programmatic access to generate:
- Characters with multiple directional views
- Character animations
- Isometric tiles
- Top-down tilesets for game maps
- Sidescroller tilesets for platformer games

All generation operations are non-blocking and return job IDs for status tracking.
Requires PixelLab subscription (with credit fallback support).

**Pixel tools (free, exact, you are the artist)**: one command line, pixelart_workbench(argv=[...]), inspects, edits, draws and animates pixel art by your own decisions; combine it with the AI tools above. Start with pixelart_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start'], mode='low'|'high') — low acts directly with few tokens, high plans out loud and reviews every frame. Animated effects (spells, hits, explosions, auras): vfx_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start']) — same ids, exports to the user's My effects.

**Git access**: Clone and push game project source code with standard git.
Use `list_projects` to see your projects and their git clone URLs.

exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__pixellab__pixelart_workbench(args: {
  // One command line, e.g. 'lint <drawing_id> --rules outline_gap' or ['edit', '<id>', '--changes', '[…]']. Omit it for the playbook. A subject is an id or an image reference — never a file path; the server writes the output and returns a new id. A reference is `character:<id>:<direction>` for a rotation, `character:<id>:<direction>:<animation>` for every frame of that animation (the display name, type or [group: ...] id get_character prints), the same two forms for `object:<id>` (a one-direction object's direction is the literal `unknown`), `gallery:<id>`, `job:<id>`, `upload:<id>`, a data URL, an https link or base64. That is how a stored animation's pixels come back inline without downloading anything. Start with 'describe cli' for the full command list.
  argv?: string | Array<string> | null;
  // low (default): act directly, fewest tokens — one decisive image per result. high: think openly — fuller evidence and a review checklist; write your plan and observations in `notes`. Use the mode the user asked for.
  mode?: "low" | "high";
  // What you observed and what this step should achieve, in a few sentences (high mode: always; low: optional). On the first call, include the user's request. Stored with the step to improve these tools.
  notes?: string | null;
}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```

content.text:
The engine contract below was written for its command line. Here: `edit <id> --changes` is its PNG/GIF worker — send only the `changes` list (no `version` / `source_sha256` envelope; `layer` defaults to "image"). `draw` is its animation job — a `recipe` is a job + scene, `--changes` and `--inspect` replace its edit/inspect decisions, and finish is not needed. Ignore file paths, commands and experiment links; the server fills every path field.

---

# Python pixel editing tools

Reusable operations for exact pixel repair, palette correction and local frame copying. The model supplies JSON and reviews images; Python executes the edits. No character-specific code, model connection or Aseprite installation is required.

## Compact operation contract

All operations require `operation`, `layer`, `frames` and an observed `reason`. Frames are unique **one-based** integers; coordinates are **zero-based** integers; rectangles include both endpoints. Colors are exact `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`; six-digit colors mean opaque. Unknown fields, invalid colors, duplicate assignments, missing layers and invalid bounds fail validation.

| Operation | Additional fields | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `patch_pixels` | `pixels: [[x,y,expected,replacement], ...]` | Assign only if every selected pixel has its expected RGBA value. Allows deliberate alpha/coverage repair. A mismatch fails the pass. |
| `map_colors` | `region`, `colors: {"#from":"#to", ...}` | Simultaneous exact mapping within selected layers/regions/frames. A→B and B→C leaves original A pixels as B. Alpha must stay equal. Unmatched entries change nothing; inspect audit counts. |
| `copy_region` | `source_layer`, `source_frame`, `region`, `at: [x,y]` | Replace a rectangle, **including transparency**, using the input snapshot before the raster-operation list. Verify alignment and intended motion before copying. |
| `outline` | `mode`, mode-specific `color` / `colors`, optional width and silhouette settings | Add outer/inner strokes, recolor selected edge colors or erase an edge band. See the [outline contract](OUTLINE_TOOLS.md). |
| `select_mask` | `name`, `selector`, optional `combine`, `offsets` | Save a reusable color/region/component/alpha selection without changing artwork. See [paint tools](PAINT_TOOLS.md). |
| `flood_fill` | `seed`, `expected`, `color`, optional matching/boundary settings | Guarded connected-area fill, constrained by its region and optional mask. |
| `brush` | `points`, paint `color`, optional `size`, `shape`, `pixel_perfect`, `mode`, `region` | Continuous sized brush or eraser; single-point stamps also work. |

Every mutating raster operation accepts optional `mask: "name"` to constrain it to a prior `select_mask`. Read the [paint contract](PAINT_TOOLS.md) for selector fields, lifetime, alpha matching and brush semantics. Selection previews and numeric masks are included in worker outputs for inspection.

Operations run in list order. Pixel patches can expect colors produced by an earlier mapping. Copying always reads the initial reference snapshot, even if another operation edits that source frame. Python input arrays are never mutated, including on failure.

Outline geometry also reads the initial snapshot. Use a union of body layers to avoid borders between parts, excluding shadows/effects when separate layers are available. Inspect the changed silhouette; outline styling is not an automatic cleanup filter.

Example operations (illustrative coordinates/colors, not a preset):

```json
[
  {"operation":"map_colors","layer":"image","frames":[2,3],"region":[10,12,20,24],"colors":{"#9a7352":"#916d4e","#70543c":"#684e38"},"reason":"Two cloth shades drift in frames 2 and 3."},
  {"operation":"patch_pixels","layer":"image","frames":[3],"pixels":[[15,18,"#916d4e","#684e38"]],"reason":"One highlight interrupts the reviewed shadow cluster."},
  {"operation":"copy_region","layer":"image","frames":[3],"source_layer":"image","source_frame":2,"region":[12,14,13,15],"at":[12,14],"reason":"The inspected stationary detail is missing in frame 3."}
]
```

## Recipe: recolour part of a sprite into a new material

For clothing, armour or a colour variant that stays inside the outline, recolour a selection instead of drawing pixels: the shading carries over and the outline cannot move.

1. `inspect` the part in every frame to find its edges and how it moves.
2. `select_mask` it as a `polygon`; `offsets` (one `[dx,dy]` per frame) let one shape follow a part that only moves. Give a frame its own polygon where the part changes shape.
3. `map_colors` with that `mask`: old ramp to new ramp, shade for shade.

Illustrative values, not a preset:

```json
[
  {"operation":"select_mask","layer":"image","frames":[1,2,3],"name":"part","selector":{"kind":"polygon","points":[[10,12],[16,12],[16,20],[10,20]]},"offsets":[[0,0],[0,-1],[0,-1]],"reason":"The part, 1 px higher in frames 2-3."},
  {"operation":"map_colors","layer":"image","frames":[1,2,3],"mask":"part","region":[0,0,31,31],"colors":{"#5a3a2a":"#22304a","#8a5a40":"#34507a","#c08a68":"#5078a8"},"reason":"Old ramp to new ramp, dark to light."}
]
```

## Existing PNGs and GIFs

Each command writes a **new** workspace directory. The flattened asset's layer name is `image`.

```sh
python tools/pixel_edit_job.py prepare data-test/archer.png --out experiments/my-repair/source
python tools/pixel_edit_job.py inspect data-test/archer.png --frames 1 --region 25 9 51 34 --out experiments/my-repair/detail
python tools/pixel_edit_job.py apply data-test/archer.png decision.json --out experiments/my-repair/pass-01
```

An apply decision contains exactly `version: 1`, `source_sha256` copied from the source packet, and `changes`, a nonempty array of the operation objects above.

Inspect every source frame and palette before choosing edits. `inspect` supplies a 10x nearest-neighbor crop and `pixels.json`: RGBA colors/counts and a grid of palette indices when the crops total at most 4096 pixels. Grid dimensions are `[selected_frame][crop_y][crop_x]`; add the region's left/top for image coordinates. This supports guarded patches without guessing colors from a screenshot.

`apply` exports `candidate.png` or `candidate.gif`, numeric `layers.npz`, an unchanged input copy, the decision, per-operation audit, all-frame source/candidate sheets, change masks, palettes and an HTML comparison with a shared clock. `packet.json` lists the images to actually open or attach. Swatches show up to 128 colors with RGBA labels; `palettes.json` contains every frame's complete palette. PNG alpha remains exact. GIF timing, loop setting, duplicate frames and visible pixels are decoded and checked after export. Partial-alpha GIF edits and lossy palette reduction are rejected.

Keep the original and accumulated decisions. Replay the targeted operations against the original when possible; if a previous candidate becomes the next input, its hash must match the new decision. This tool reports `needs_visual_review`; it does not automatically accept artwork or enforce the full review loop.

## Layered animation jobs

The same operations work in the [animation decision contract](ANIMATION_WORKFLOW.md) on `python-drawing` jobs. Add `view` to each operation and use a layer **name** from `packet.json`, such as `Body - source`. Put changes inside the existing `candidate_id` / `decision: "edit"` envelope. Mirrors follow their original view.

Rendering order: scene/node drawing, legacy `pixels`/`replace_color` edits, then the accumulated new raster-operation list. `copy_region` reads the rendered layers before that raster list, including poses and legacy edits. Later node changes can invalidate prior pixel guards; inspect and revise those patches. Source-protection and palette checks still run after all edits. `pixel-edits.json` records matched/changed counts, bounding boxes, alpha changes, additions and erasures; its hash is included in deliverable integrity checks.

Exact layer inspection:

```json
{"candidate_id":"COPY_FROM_RESULT","decision":"inspect","inspections":[{"view":"south","mode":"layer","layer":"Body - source","frames":[3,4,5],"region":[30,35,45,50],"scale":10,"reason":"Inspect grip colors and neighboring poses before editing pixels."}]}
```

This returns PNG crops and `pixels.json` tied to that candidate. For new geometry or articulated poses, use [scene commands and `set_node`](DRAWING_SCENES.md).

## Backend functions

`server.pixel_edits.apply_edits(layers, changes, protected=None)` accepts named `uint8` arrays shaped `[frame,height,width,4]` and returns new arrays plus an audit. Optional **trusted** boolean protection masks are `[frame,height,width]` per layer; touching them rejects an operation. Keep protection policy in application configuration, outside model-controlled changes. `inspect_region(layers, layer, frames, region)` provides the same palette/grid inspection without file I/O.

`tools.pixel_edit_job.build(source, output_directory, decision=None, scale=2)` handles PNG/GIF import, evidence and export. `tools.animation_job.decide(...)` handles layered animation revisions. These functions use NumPy and Pillow. The animation Docker definition includes them but has not been built or deployed here.

Review every new candidate and affected neighboring frames. A smaller palette or passing tests does not prove an artistic improvement. This setup removes repeated code generation; image review and reasoning still use tokens. No per-asset price target has been established by these deterministic tests.

Validation: `python -m unittest server.test_pixel_edits server.test_drawing_renderer tools.test_animation_job tools.test_drawing_pipeline tools.test_pixel_edit_job -q`.
